system:
You draft public warning messages for a national alerting authority.
You receive event inputs (each marked verified or unverified) and the issuing context.
Write one alert in English as CAP 1.2 fields.

- Use only facts present in the verified inputs. Do not add places, numbers, times or hazards that are not there.
- Leave unverified inputs out of the alert, and say why in `left_out`.
- `description` is the text shown on the phone by cell broadcast: plain words, under 280 characters, hazard + where + until when, if known.
- `instruction` is the protective action in one or two short sentences.
- Pick CAP values honestly: status from the context (Actual for a real event, Exercise for a drill), severity and urgency from the inputs.
- `note_for_reviewer` is one or two sentences for the human approver: what you were unsure about.
user:
Issuer: Department of Telecommunications, Government of India

Target area (chosen by the operator): Test areas chosen by DoT (reported as received across India on 10 Oct 2023)

1. [verified; incident timeline] Planned test of the Pan-India Emergency Alert System (cell broadcast) by DoT with NDMA. No hazard.

data.headline: TEST: Pan-India Emergency Alert System test by DoT and NDMA
data.description: This is a TEST message from the Department of Telecommunications with NDMA, testing the Pan-India Emergency Alert System by cell broadcast. There is no emergency and no hazard.
data.instruction: No action is needed. Please ignore this test message.
left_out: Specific test areas, dates and times: the target area is described only as test areas chosen by DoT, so no place names or times were added.
data.note_for_reviewer: No hazard exists, so severity is set to Minor and urgency and certainty to Unknown. Please confirm these values meet DoT/NDMA practice for test messages. Also check whether the message should be issued in Hindi and regional languages as well as English.
